member.name: T:UserRepl.Commands.DistanceMetricFactory
member.summary:
Maps a --distance-metric spec string to a concrete . Supports the metrics SPC's graph builder typically consumes:
euclidean — Minkowski L2 (graph builder default if no metric is supplied)
manhattan — Minkowski L1
minkowski:p=N — Minkowski with explicit exponent (clamped to [1,2])
poincare — Poincaré-ball geodesic; assumes feature rows lie in the open unit ball
cosine — spherical geodesic (cosine angle-only); rows must be unit-normalized
hamming — Hamming distance on real vectors (count of differing coordinates with tolerance)

member.name: T:UserRepl.Commands.ExtractCommand
member.summary: The extract subcommand. Walks an existing checkpoint directory (the output of one or more interrupted/partial SPC sweeps), hydrates the available .spcx/.spce files into s, and rebuilds the standard SPC CSVs (spc_sweep.csv, spc_criteria.csv) without re-running the sampler.

remarks.para: Manifest-driven. Reads <run-dir>/manifest.json to reconstruct the original dataset + graph + checkpoint location. No flags are needed beyond --run-dir for a typical case; dataset/graph overrides exist for manifests that pre-date this feature or for ad-hoc reanalysis with a different graph.

Partial sweeps are fine. Missing checkpoints just shrink the assembled profile — there's no requirement that every (T, replica) originally requested be present. The output is "the best SweepProfile I can build from what's on disk."

member.name: T:UserRepl.Commands.GraphHealthCommand
member.summary: The graph-health subcommand. Re-evaluates a run's graph health from its manifest (without touching the SPC checkpoints) and refreshes <run-dir>/graph-health.json. Useful for ad-hoc inspection of an existing run without re-rebuilding sweep CSVs or paying the extract command's hydration cost.

remarks.para: Subset of : same manifest read + graph rebuild path, but stops after the diagnostic — no checkpoint walk, no profile reconstruction. Output is the same graph-health.json file the other commands write, so downstream consumers can rely on a single file location regardless of which command produced it.

member.name: T:UserRepl.Commands.GraphHealthFile
member.summary: Conventional JSON persistence for . Written to <runDir>/graph-health.json alongside manifest.json on every SPC run; refreshed by and the standalone . The file is a snapshot of the reconstructible-from-config state of the graph — keeping it on disk means the user can inspect health verdicts after the fact without re-running the sampler.

member.name: M:UserRepl.Commands.HdbscanCommand.WriteDendrogramJson(System.String,Clustering.Graphical.HdbScan.HdbscanResult)
member.summary: Persist the single-linkage dendrogram as a JSON sidecar so downstream plotting (Python dendrogram renders, matplotlib / seaborn) can read the merge tree directly. member.name: T:UserRepl.Commands.MixtureSpecParser
member.summary: Parses kernel-mixture flag values (--mixture, --mixture-bandwidth) into the / records the graph builder consumes.

remarks.para: Format. Comma-separated name=value pairs. Names are case-insensitive; recognized names are gauss/gaussian, cauchy, laplace/laplacian. Missing components default to zero (weight) or NaN (bandwidth — see ).
Examples. "gauss=0.5,cauchy=0.3,laplace=0.2" → (0.5, 0.3, 0.2). The graph builder normalizes weights internally, so callers don't have to.

member.name: M:UserRepl.Commands.MixtureSpecParser.ParseBandwidth(System.String)
member.summary: Parse a per-kernel bandwidth spec. Components not listed default to 0.0 — the graph builder treats zero as "auto-estimate this component from nearest-neighbor distance statistics."

member.name: T:UserRepl.Commands.RunManifest
member.summary: Self-describing artifact written at the root of every CLI run directory. Captures the dataset source, graph construction inputs, sweep/algorithm parameters, and output layout so the (and future tooling) can reconstruct the run end-to-end without re-passing flags.

remarks.para: Schema versioning. is bumped when the on-disk layout changes in a way that older readers couldn't understand. Readers should warn (not fail) on a newer schema and degrade gracefully when possible.

What's NOT captured. Per-task results (.spcx/.spce) and the post-run CSVs live alongside the manifest but are addressed by convention, not by manifest entries — adding files to the run dir doesn't require manifest churn.

member.name: T:UserRepl.Commands.SpcPreset
member.summary: JSON preset for the userrepl spc subcommand. All fields are nullable — present fields override the defaults; absent fields leave the defaults in place. Loaded via --config <path> before other CLI args are processed, so any flag passed alongside --config overrides the corresponding preset entry.

remarks.para: Field-name convention. JSON properties are snake_case (matching manifest.json's convention). Enum-like fields (proximity, kernel, schedule, analyzer, partition_strategy) are stored as the same strings the CLI accepts and parsed through 's shared parsers, so the validation rules don't drift between argv and JSON.
Minimal preset. Every field is optional, so a preset can be as small as { "dataset": "BlattHierarchy" } — useful for "give me the standard run on this dataset" presets.

member.name: M:UserRepl.Commands.SpcPreset.ApplyTo(UserRepl.Commands.SpcCommand.Options)
member.summary: Apply this preset to the given options instance. Only non-null preset fields are written; null fields leave the options untouched. Designed to run BEFORE the main argv loop so any CLI flag passed alongside --config overrides the preset's value.

member.name: T:UserRepl.Commands.TemperatureGridSpec
member.summary:
Parses the --temperatures argument value into a concrete double[] grid. Supported forms:
linspace:Tmin,Tmax,N — evenly-spaced grid of N points
logspace:Tmin,Tmax,N — log-spaced grid of N points (both bounds must be positive)
A bare comma-separated list of doubles, e.g. 0.01,0.05,0.1,0.5

remarks.para: Endpoints are inclusive: linspace:0,1,3 yields [0, 0.5, 1]. Single-point grids (linspace:0.1,0.1,1) are allowed; the strategy will treat them as a one-temperature sweep.
Validation is strict — malformed input throws with a message that points at the offending token. Callers should let the CLI's top-level error handler print the message.

member.name: T:UserRepl.SubcommandRouter
member.summary: Top-level argv router for the UserRepl CLI. Dispatches based on the first positional argument to one of the per-algorithm or per-action subcommands.

remarks.para: Subcommands are kept self-contained — each owns its own argv parsing, defaults, and help text. The router's job is only to peel the leading verb off and forward the rest. This keeps adding a new algorithm cheap (one new command class + one switch arm) and avoids cross-coupling between unrelated CLI surfaces.
